title: Vamana
hook: when someone you love loses everything and you can't fix it
tomorrow: the promised son is tiny. so what does he ask the king for?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Narasimha's last scene: a hand on a boy's head, and Prahlada's one wish spent on his father. Now the story moves on two generations, to Prahlada's grandson.

There's a particular helplessness in watching someone you love lose something you can't get back for them: a job, a place on a team, a home. In the Bhagavata Purana, that's Aditi. Her sons are the gods, and they've just lost heaven. Prahlada's grandson, Bali, a generous king of the asuras, has taken it, and the gods are in hiding. Aditi can't fight him. She can't fix it. So she sits at home, and grieves.
screen: `YOU CAN'T FIX IT FOR THEM.` → `HER SONS HAVE LOST HEAVEN.` → `SHE SITS, AND GRIEVES.`

segments.voice: Then her husband, the sage Kashyapa, comes home and finds the house gone quiet. He listens. He doesn't promise to fix it, and he doesn't tell her to stop being sad. He gives her something to do: a vow of worship to Vishnu, kept day after day, with milk at its center. The text calls it payovrata, the milk vow. It's small, it's steady, and it's hers. So Aditi keeps it, the same simple worship, every day of the vow. And at the end, Vishnu appears to her and makes a promise: he will be born as her son. When that son arrives, he's small. A boy, a dwarf, a young student who, in the telling, is given an umbrella and a water pot. His name is Vamana, the small one. Here's what the story offers on a week like this one. When the loss is too big to fix, Aditi doesn't storm heaven. She does one small thing, steadily, and keeps doing it. And the help, when it comes, comes the way nobody would have planned it: small enough to hold.
screen: `HE LISTENS. HE DOESN'T FIX IT.` · `PAYOVRATA: THE MILK VOW.` · `ONE SMALL THING, STEADILY.` · `THE HELP COMES SMALL.` · then, large: `SMALL ENOUGH TO HOLD.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person you love who's carrying a loss you can't fix. Name, silently, what you wish for them; then what stands in the way; then one small, steady thing you could do, a weekly call, a meal, sitting with them. Give each of the three a few slow breaths.
Vamana: Vishnu as the small one, a young dwarf student, born to Aditi after her steady vow.
Your line: Vamana. When Aditi couldn't fix it, she kept one small thing steady. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Hindus keep a vrata, a vow of fasting or simple worship over set days, for a family member in trouble; keeping the vow steadily is itself the offering.
